artboards.title: Spending — dark, bars and a suppressed comparison

annotations.text: Direction A, retuned to your steer. Warm graphite rather than Apple's cool silver — same era, different hand. 33px rows. The loudest block changes with state: work outstanding on the left board, caught up on the third. Pick a grey on the Which grey? board below and I'll commit the whole system to it.
The two decisions still open: which grey family, and confirmation that the constrained accents still read as the six colours you chose. The ladder sheet is the contract underneath both.
The measured critique. Every number here came from the token file or the component source, not from the screenshots.
Not chosen, kept for reference. B's margin-gutter group labels and C's density are both still liftable into A if you want them.

Does the system generalise? Two pages it was not designed against: a 24-row ledger and a page made of charts. Three things had to change, and none of them broke the ladder.

1. Sign colour does not scale. Nearly every row on a ledger is negative; 22 red numbers reads as 22 errors. Colour now marks the MINORITY sign — the minus carries the dominant one.
2. The accent was doing chart duty. SpendingBreakdown fills every bar with --color-accent, which cannot also mean "the one live thing". Bars move to a neutral --bar-ink; accent marks only the category you drilled into.
3. Zebra striping is gone. The hairlines already separate rows at ΔL .115, so the stripe was a second answer to a solved question. This pass's named deletion.
Both themes, because a system that only holds in one is not a system. The day bands, the coverage strip, the block bars, the hatch and the suppressed comparison all sit on the same rungs in both.
